findings: Expert SOP S18 host panels and ~30s expectation do not include a measured full-inventory fallback budget; A1 section7 explicitly defines that fallback while panels are absent.
Current HiMat always selects package_pan_allele; host metadata does not narrow the panel. This run expands to 23711 alleles across species.
Engineering caps 20/15 and balanced paired batches yield 738 sequential child jobs; each executes MHC I then II. No expert requirement fixes these batch caps.
101 hash-verified runtime receipts show MHC I dominates native elapsed time. No evidence of repeated retries or long inter-batch queue waits in these successful batches.
8h parent timeout clamps N05 to the entire remaining deadline, leaving no budget for WARNING+continue fallback or downstream work.
Conditional workflow tail creates a fresh wt_netmhc for the identical original sequence, plus variant N05 evaluations; these were not reached in the stopped run.
limitations: No new native benchmark; cannot separate native model loading from inference within channel timings.
CPU limit is 2; historical CPU utilization/throttling not measured, so increasing cores is not a proven fix.
Host-specific allele panel remains missing in expert package. Cannot select arbitrary representative alleles or promise 30-second full inventory.
